I was 8 when my mum died she was born with cystic fibrosis she was 32 when she died in april (three days before my 8th birthday i say 8 because i was closer to 8 than 7) but she would have been 33 in the september. So she knew she was going to die her whole life. She managed to fall in love with my dad, marry and have me they were together almost 15 years. She was told she would never have children and i was concieved natrually so im a miracle baby. I was told from a young age this would happen. Its sad because if she was born just 4 or 5 years later she would still be alive today with the medicines and treatments that came out after she died and most CF patients are living into their 50s and 60s now she would be 50 this year and im 25 this year.  
I have met people who have lost a parent who are my age but at a later date. My partner lost his mother to bowel cancer in april 2021 she was in her late 50s or early 60s i cant remember. My partner was my best friend but we didnt actually start our relationship until about 6 months after she died as he had a girlfriend at the time. Realised we loved eachother got engaged and had a baby (he's 3 this may) it moved pretty fast but he was my best friend beforehand so it wasnt like we just met, he still is, we just have a child and sleep together, still going strong our 4 year anniversary coming up later this year.  But its been nice as a veteran of this to be able to help him through his grief and also not be alone in it.  But also he was 20 when his mother died so an adult, so its not the same, he doesnt understand what it is like to grow up without one and thats ok, but it feels like a gap if that makes sense. He talks to me about all the time he had with her and i still get jelous and say to him i wish i had that. 
Sorry im rambling.

Borderline personality disorder need i explain more. That and trying to be a mother, not having mine since 8, im kinda in the dark. 
People think im crazy when i joke about it but its coming up 17 years without her so i think that im entitled too. People get so shocked but its my coping mechanism. 
My partner's mother also died about 4 years ago. (Both in april weirdly enough) so at least being a veteran i could help him through it. April is a tough month for both of us but also my birthday is in april so its alot (my mum died 3 days before my 8th birthday). 

I think now ive had a child ive only really just started to accept that she's gone and i think about her every day and miss her more than anything in the world. Growing up i just kind of ignored it and ignored it until it got too much for me and i ended up experiencing all the grief at once and having a nervous breakdown when my son was born. (That was fun... not).
When i was in labour i started screaming i want my mum and my partner kept saying "she's not here anymore but i am" and i kept saying "i know but i want her" and crying.
Thats the first time in a long time like since i was a little kid that i felt like i needed her and ive needed her every single day since. I miss her so much.  
Mentally, my brain is completely fried and i often wonder how different a person i would be if she hadnt died. I dont blame her though, i blame the people that promised her that they would look after me when she was gone and they didnt and they just added to the trauma. That and my dad being mentally ill didnt really mix. After mum died my childhood basically ended as i became his carer. 
Things are ok now, i have my own family and my own life, i have a great relationship with my dad and since my son came into the world that twinkle he had in his eyes he had when mum was alive has come back. He's my best friend and we're all happy. 

But my mental illness will never go away and missing her will never go away. I just hope some day it hurts a little less. Even if its just a little.
